newsitem.title: USA: "Star Wars" shines brightest at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Star Wars" shines brightest at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Star Wars," the sci-fi extravaganza that last week reclaimed its title as the highest grossing film in U.S. history, fended off several strong new releases to lead the box office for the third weekend, according to studio estimates released on Monday.

Meanwhile, several movies featured prominently at last Tuesday's Oscar nominees announcement saw their fortunes improve considerably. Among them, the Australian movie "Shine," with seven nominations, entered the top 10 for the first time after almost three months in limited release.
The top 10 contained four new releases, headed by Clint Eastwood's White House thriller "Absolute Power," which opened in second with $16.8 million.

But none of the movies was a match for "Star Wars," originally released in 1977 and now reissued with several minutes of extra footage. It earned an estimated $21.3 million during the Friday-to-Monday Presidents Holiday weekend, taking its lifetime gross to $421.3 million.
It reclaimed its title last Thursday when it passed the $399.8 million earned by the 1982 movie "E.T. The Extraterrestrial."

"Star Wars," which is released by News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox, averaged $10,124 from 2,104 screens over the weekend. The reissue has earned $98.6 million, and its strongest competition is expected next weekend when its 1980 sequel "The Empire Strikes Back" comes out again.

"Absolute Power," which is released by Sony Corp.'s Columbia Pictures, averaged $6,542 from 2,568 screens. Eastwood, who also directed the movie, plays a thief caught up in the murder of the President's mistress. The movie received modestly good reviews, with a Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC showing that 17 liked it, 14 did not and 12 were mixed.

"Jerry Maguire," in seventh place, was the highest grossing Oscar-nominated film at the weekend with $5.3 million for four days. This represents a 48 percent increase from its three-day total last weekend when it was fourth. The Sony-released movie has five nominations including best picture, best actor for Tom Cruise and best supporting actor for Cuba Gooding Jr.
The awards will be handed out on March 24.

"The English Patient," which headed the list with 12 Oscar nominations, was steady in eighth with $5.0 million, which represented a 123 percent increase from last weekend. The wartime drama added 73 screens to 1,115, taking its average to $4,484. After just over three months in release, it has earned $48.1 million. Its nominations include best picture, best director and screenplay adaptation for Anthony Minghella, best actor for Ralph Fiennes, best actress for Kristin Scott Thomas and best supporting actress for Juliette Binoche.

"Shine" was 10th with $3.5 million, an increase of 240 percent over last weekend when it was 15th. The movie added 537 screens, taking its total to 851. It averaged $4,113 and has earned a total of $20 million. Its nominations include best picture, best director for Scott Hicks, best actor for Geoffrey Rush and best supporting actor for Armin Mueller-Stahl.
"The English Patient" is released by Miramax Films, a unit of Walt Disney Co., while "Shine" is released by Fine Line Features, a unit of Time Warner Inc..

Last weekend's No. 2, "Dante's Peak," slipped to third in its second round with $14.3 million and an average of $5,244. The volcano disaster movie, which is released by Seagram Co. Ltd.'s Universal Pictures, has earned $36.9 million to date.

Opening in fourth was the Chevy Chase comedy "Vegas Vacation," which was not screened for critics prior to its release. It earned $13.1 million from $2,054 screens for a surprisingly strong average of $6,378. The movie is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner.
The other new releases included "Fools Rush In" at fifth with $10 million and "That Darn Cat" at sixth with $6.5 million.
